title: Decide spec-method defaults: per-user updates, expire_message
description:
Follow-up from JMAP-ic0j.26 sweep (policy: bd memory spec-method-defaults, AGENTS.md 'Default bodies on spec-semantic backend methods'). Three defaults are judgment calls, not clear 'wrong data on the wire' cases:

1. crate-jmap-tasks-server/src/backend.rs TasksBackend::update_task_per_user delegates to update_object. draft-ietf-jmap-tasks-06 §4.5.1: a per-user-only patch MUST NOT change the shared 'updated' timestamp. Correct for single-user backends; wrong in multi-user deployments if update_object bumps 'updated'. Previously tracked by JMAP-ops7.23 and JMAP-h47t.15, which were each closed as a duplicate of the other, so it is currently untracked. MemoryBackend relies on the default.
2. crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/backend.rs CalendarsBackend::update_per_user_properties: same shape as (1), sibling of the tasks method (draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-26 per-user properties).
3. crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs ChatBackend::expire_message defaults to Ok(()) with no in-crate caller; an application scheduler drives it. With the default, expired messages stay visible to Message/get.

Options per item: (a) drop default (required method, explicit overrides in MemoryBackend/mocks); (b) keep default, tighten rustdoc to MUST override for multi-user / expiry. Recommendation: (a) for 1 and 2 in one canonical-template sweep; (b) for 3 since the crate never calls it.
